sections.commitments:
- Software under Apache 2.0; chip RTL and board design files under CERN-OHL-W, except the bus fabric, USB PHY and analog blocks, which do not process data.
- Pinned targets: Release firmware rebuilds bit-identically from source, the full recovery phrase never appears on the Ostros screen, and no secret is shared across devices.
- Ostros works with any Ethereum app and does not require a proprietary companion app.
- Public vulnerability disclosure process; fixes ship as signed, reproducible firmware.
- CrossBar maintains the grant deliverables for at least 12 months after the final milestone (security fixes, firmware updates, review of outside pull requests).
- CrossBar publishes the IRIS rig design, software and Devcon 8 reference images under open licenses.
sections.in_scope:
- **Attestation:** Each Ostros can prove it carries a genuine Daric chip, set up in a new factory personalization flow. The split recovery phrase and the app loader both build on it.
  - Technical: A key generated inside the chip at personalization, checked against a published CrossBar root, as a per-device certificate or anonymous attestation (scheme chosen during the grant).
- **Clear signing:** Ostros shows Ethereum transactions in plain language (ERC-7730), or the verifiable digest (ERC-8213) when no descriptor exists.
- **Web companion:** Connects Ostros to any Ethereum app through WalletConnect.
  - Technical: USB or Bluetooth; the device decodes and displays each request itself, so the companion never decides what the owner sees.
- **Owner verification:** A public guide and tool to rebuild the firmware, match its hash and check the attestation.
- **Split recovery phrase:** Features a 24-word phrase: 12 words show on the Ostros screen and 12 go to the owner's computer over a connection the computer checks comes from a genuine Daric chip. An implant on the screen never sees the full phrase, so an attacker needs both an implant and malware on the computer (method by Nicolas Bacca, Devcon 8).
  - Technical: The computer accepts its 12 words only after checking that the session key is signed by the device's attestation key. The 12 words an implant could see leave more than 120 bits of the phrase unknown.
- **App loader and developer kit:** Outside teams install security apps without rebuilding the firmware, with an emulator and system API documentation.
  - Technical: Each app runs in its own Xous process, isolated by the MMU, under a permission model that limits what each app can reach.
sections.out_scope:
- Planned follow-on initiative: (1) the openable device, and (2) research into Daric chip inspection in the Ostros package.
- Drivers not needed for these features (power management, fingerprint, NFC, vibrator, LED), the app store website and MPC on the RISC-V core: CrossBar builds these with its own funds.
- Apps for other chains (Bitcoin and others).

sections.why:
- **Screen implants.** In October 2026, Ledger confirmed a hidden implant in at least one device sold through a reseller. The implant read the recovery phrase off the Ledger device's screen during setup and sent it out over a mobile network. Reported losses exceed $86 million (BleepingComputer, Ledger).
- **Blind signing.** In February 2025, Bybit lost about $1.5 billion after its Safe signers approved a malicious upgrade they could not read on their devices (BlockSec).
- **No way to check.** Most hardware wallet owners cannot verify that their device runs the published firmware on a genuine chip.

After this grant, an Ostros owner creates a recovery phrase that a screen implant never sees in full, reads Ethereum transactions in plain language before signing, and confirms their firmware and chip are genuine.

This grant is one step toward a goal of a hardware wallet that owners can verify end to end, from an open-source chip through open software to a device they can open and inspect. CrossBar builds both the chip and the wallet, so this goal can be reached. Any hardware wallet can reuse the split recovery phrase method, the attestation design and the owner verification tool, the way distributions build on Linux. A follow-on initiative will (1) make the device openable, and (2) let owners inspect the chip inside their own wallet.
sections.why_grant:
- **The chip:** Daric, CrossBar's security chip with published RTL, SDK and documentation, features a 350 MHz RISC-V core with an MMU, 4 MB of ReRAM, crypto accelerators, a true random number generator, a key store, glitch sensors and a security mesh. Its post-quantum library (ML-DSA, ML-KEM) is NIST CAVP-validated on the RISC-V core.
- **The software:** Xous runs on Ostros with a fully open bootloader, core drivers, an e-ink UI, seed generation and key management. The firmware build is deterministic.
- **The Ethereum signer:** The shared Ethereum signer (https://github.com/ethereum/ethereum-app) runs on Ostros hardware with verifiable signing (ERC-8213), demoed at Devcon 8.
- **Developers:** The Founders Edition ships to developers in late November 2026, and teams have applied to build apps on it. At Devcon 8, 196 developers signed up for CrossBar's Dabao hackathon and picked up a free board with the same die, so they already use the RISC-V, Rust and Xous tools Ostros needs.
- **In use and openly reviewed:** Ostros builds on the open Xous environment (OS and secure boot), where findings from public reviews of the Daric die are fixed. The Baochip version of that die shipped in every DEF CON 34 badge (August 2026). At Devcon 8, CrossBar guided about 250 attendees one by one through IRIS inspections, on their own chip or on a demo chip.

The secure chip and the operating system already exist, so the grant covers the security features and their adoption.

initiative.summary: Ostros™ is CrossBar's hardware wallet, open from the chip to the apps. It runs on Daric, CrossBar's open-core RISC-V security chip, and the Rust-based Xous operating system. This grant adds chip attestation, clear signing, a recovery phrase a screen implant cannot read, an owner check that firmware and chip are genuine, an independent security review, and an app loader for outside security apps. The grant is paid out as wallets add Ostros support, owners verify their own devices, and outside teams build security apps on it.
initiative.title: Ostros: an open-source hardware wallet on CrossBar's security chip, against screen implants and blind signing
